1	"""Single-file SQL query layer.
2	
3	Public API:
4	
5	* :func:`query_file` -- run a ``SELECT ... FROM input [WHERE ...]`` query
6	  against one columnar file and return a :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.Table`
7	* :func:`query_files` -- run a statement (optionally with one equi-join)
8	  against a table-name to path mapping
9	* :func:`explain_file` / :func:`explain_files` -- parse, bind and plan the
10	  same statements without executing them; only file metadata is read
11	* :class:`QuerySyntaxError` -- lexical / grammatical errors
12	* :class:`QueryValidationError` -- unknown columns, wrong table name,
13	  type-incompatible comparisons, invalid aggregate use
14	
15	The accepted grammar (keywords case-insensitive)::
16	
17	    query       := SELECT [DISTINCT] select_item (',' select_item)*
18	                   FROM ident [WHERE expr] [GROUP BY ident (',' ident)*]
19	                   [HAVING expr]
20	                   [ORDER BY order_item (',' order_item)*]
21	                   [LIMIT uint]
22	    select_item := '*' | ident | agg_name '(' ('*' | ident) ')'
23	                   | scalar_expr AS alias
24	    order_item  := (ident | agg_name '(' ('*' | ident) ')')
25	                   [ASC | DESC] [NULLS FIRST | NULLS LAST]
26	    expr       := or_expr
27	    or_expr     := and_expr (OR and_expr)*
28	    and_expr    := cmp_expr (AND cmp_expr)*
29	    cmp_expr    := not_factor (cmp_op not_factor)?
30	    not_factor  := NOT not_factor | postfix
31	    postfix     := scalar_expr (IS [NOT] NULL)?
32	    scalar_expr := term (('+' | '-') term)*
33	    term        := factor (('*' | '/') factor)*
34	    factor      := ('+' | '-') factor | atom
35	    atom        := '(' expr ')' | operand
36	                | CASE WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr
37	                  (WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr)*
38	                  (ELSE scalar_expr)? END
39	    operand     := ident | literal
40	    literal     := TRUE | FALSE | [+-]? int64 | [+-]? finite float64
41	                   | single-quoted utf8
42	
43	The supported aggregates are ``COUNT(*)``, ``COUNT(ident)`` and
44	``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` applied to one column.  Without
45	GROUP BY the projection may contain aggregate expressions only; with
46	GROUP BY it may additionally contain the grouped columns.  A bare ``*``
47	must not be mixed with aggregates or grouping.  Aggregates are not
48	allowed inside WHERE, may not be nested, and aliases are not supported
49	for bare columns or aggregate calls.
50	
51	Scalar arithmetic (parentheses, unary ``+``/``-``, binary ``+`` ``-``
52	``*`` ``/``; precedence: parentheses, unary, ``*``/``/``, ``+``/``-``)
53	is available over int64 / float64 columns and numeric literals in SELECT
54	and WHERE.  A computed SELECT expression must be named with ``AS`` (the
55	alias follows the usual identifier rules and must be unique among the
56	output names); bare columns and aggregate calls keep their existing
57	result names.  int64 ``+``/``-``/``*`` on two int64 operands yields
58	int64; any float64 operand or a division yields float64, and unary
59	operators preserve the operand type.  Any NULL operand makes the result
60	NULL; the output column is nullable iff a participating column is
61	nullable (pure constants are not).  int64 overflow, division by zero and
62	non-finite float64 results raise :class:`QueryValidationError`.  A
63	numeric expression used directly as a boolean condition is rejected with
64	:class:`QueryValidationError` as well.  Non-aggregate queries execute
65	WHERE, then compute the sort keys, stably sort, apply LIMIT and only
66	then evaluate the SELECT expressions, so filtered or truncated rows
67	never trigger division-by-zero or overflow in the projection; a
68	DISTINCT query instead evaluates the projection right after WHERE,
69	deduplicates the result rows, and only then sorts and applies LIMIT.  ORDER BY
70	may name a SELECT alias (an alias shadows an input column of the same
71	name) and sorts on the expression's result type with the usual NULL
72	placement and stability rules.  Aggregate queries do not accept scalar
73	expressions: GROUP BY keys and aggregate arguments stay plain column
74	references, and mixing a scalar expression into an aggregate query
75	raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
76	
77	``SELECT DISTINCT`` removes duplicate rows from a non-aggregate query:
78	the projection may be a star, plain columns or ``AS``-aliased scalar
79	expressions exactly as without DISTINCT, and deduplication compares the
80	full projected result row column by column after WHERE.  Two NULLs in
81	the same result column compare equal, NULL never equals a non-NULL
82	value, bool / utf8 / numeric values keep their existing comparison
83	semantics, and float64 ``0.0`` and ``-0.0`` compare equal.  Without
84	ORDER BY the surviving rows keep the order of the first occurrence of
85	each distinct result row; ORDER BY then sorts the deduplicated rows and
86	LIMIT keeps the first N.  The projection expressions are evaluated
87	only for rows that passed WHERE (and, with ORDER BY, before the sort),
88	so a division by zero, int64 overflow or non-finite float64 result that
89	actually occurs still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.  ORDER BY
90	of a DISTINCT query may name only bare columns or explicit aliases that
91	are part of the projection; an unprojected or otherwise unknown name
92	raises :class:`QueryValidationError`, and the sort direction, NULL
93	placement and stability rules are unchanged.  DISTINCT combined with
94	GROUP BY, HAVING or any aggregate projection raises
95	:class:`QueryValidationError`; ``COUNT(DISTINCT ...)`` is not part of
96	the grammar.  A missing projection, a repeated DISTINCT or a misplaced
97	DISTINCT keyword raises :class:`QuerySyntaxError` before any file is
98	opened.
99	
100	Searched CASE expressions
101	(``CASE WHEN cond THEN result [WHEN ...] [ELSE result] END``; the simple
102	``CASE value WHEN ...`` form is not supported and at least one WHEN is
103	required) are scalar operands and may be nested inside more arithmetic,
104	comparisons and other CASE expressions.  For each row the WHEN conditions
105	are tested in written order and only TRUE matches; FALSE and UNKNOWN fall
106	through, an explicit ELSE supplies the fallback and a missing ELSE yields
107	NULL.  Only the chosen result is evaluated, so division by zero, int64
108	overflow or a non-finite float64 inside an unhit branch never raises; a
109	chosen result that errors still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
110	Every reachable THEN and an explicit ELSE must share one type family:
111	int64 and float64 may mix and unify to float64, while bool and utf8 must
112	match each other exactly (any other mix raises
113	:class:`QueryValidationError`).  The result column is nullable if any
114	reachable result is nullable or the ELSE is omitted.  WHEN conditions use
115	the same boolean type check and three-valued logic as WHERE; CASE stays a
116	scalar expression, so it is rejected in aggregate arguments, GROUP BY and
117	the projection of an aggregate query just like the other scalar
118	expressions.
119	
120	Operator precedence (highest first) is NOT, comparison, AND, OR; IS [NOT]
121	NULL is a postfix of its scalar operand.  Comparison operands may be
122	column references, literals or scalar arithmetic expressions.  WHERE
123	follows SQL three-valued logic: a normal
124	comparison against NULL yields UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN propagates through the
125	logical operators, and only TRUE rows are returned.
126	
127	After WHERE, rows are grouped in GROUP BY column order (a NULL key forms
128	its own group); without an explicit ORDER BY groups come out in the order
129	of their first selected row.  An optional HAVING clause between GROUP BY
130	and ORDER BY filters the formed groups with the same boolean expression
131	grammar and three-valued logic as WHERE: its conditions combine grouping
132	columns, aggregate calls and type-compatible literals with NOT / AND / OR
133	/ comparisons / IS [NOT] NULL, only groups whose condition is TRUE are
134	kept, and aggregates named in HAVING need not appear in SELECT.  Without
135	GROUP BY HAVING filters the single global aggregate row (still produced
136	when WHERE selected no rows); with GROUP BY an empty selection yields
137	zero groups.  HAVING may not name ungrouped plain columns, ``*``, CASE,
138	scalar arithmetic or nested aggregates; it is rejected on a completely
139	non-aggregate query.  ORDER BY may only name a selected result; ASC is the
140	default, NULLs sort last regardless of direction unless NULLS FIRST /
141	NULLS LAST is given, and groups equal on every sort key keep that
142	first-row order.  LIMIT then keeps the first N groups.  Without GROUP BY
143	and aggregates an aggregate query over zero selected rows still yields one
144	output row (COUNT 0, the other aggregates NULL), unless HAVING removes it;
145	with GROUP BY it yields zero rows.
146	
147	Two-file queries (:func:`query_files`) add one equi-join to the grammar::
148	
149	    query := SELECT ... FROM left_table [join_kind JOIN right_table
150	             ON left_table.column = right_table.column] ...
151	    join_kind := INNER | LEFT
152	
153	``sources`` maps table names to file paths; only the tables referenced by
154	the statement are read.  Aliases, compound ON conditions, other join types
155	and a second join are rejected as syntax errors before any file is opened.
156	In a join query every column reference outside ``COUNT(*)`` must be
157	qualified as ``table.column`` (either part may be a double-quoted
158	identifier).  ``SELECT *`` emits the left schema followed by the right
159	schema with ``table.column`` names; explicit projections keep their
160	qualified names and aggregates keep the uppercase ``FUNC(table.column)``
161	labels.  Join keys may share a type or mix int64 with float64; NULL keys
162	never match.  INNER JOIN emits every matching combination, LEFT JOIN also
163	emits unmatched left rows with the right-side values set to NULL (the
164	right result columns are nullable).  Rows expand in left-file order, and
165	within one left row in right-file order, before WHERE / GROUP BY / HAVING
166	/ ORDER BY / LIMIT apply with their usual semantics.
167	
168	The multi-file entry points (:func:`query_files`, :func:`explain_files`)
169	take an optional ``join_strategy`` of ``"hash"`` or ``"sort_merge"``.
170	Both strategies accept the same statements and return identical column
171	descriptions, values, NULL placement and row order; they differ only in
172	how matching right rows are located (a right-key hash index versus
173	sorting both sides on the key and merging equal-key runs).  With the
174	argument omitted the historical join path is used and the explain plan
175	is unchanged; with an explicit strategy the plan's Join operator gains a
176	``strategy`` field of ``HASH`` or ``SORT_MERGE``.  A JOIN-less statement
177	accepts either strategy but gains no extra operator, and an invalid
178	strategy raises :class:`ValueError` before any source file is opened.
179	"""

253	def _validate_join_strategy(join_strategy: Any) -> str | None:
254	    """Validate the optional ``join_strategy`` argument.

257	    caller did not request one.  Any other value (including a non-string)
258	    raises :class:`ValueError`; callers run this before opening any file.

260	    if join_strategy is None:
261	        return None
262	    if not isinstance(join_strategy, str) or join_strategy not in _JOIN_STRATEGIES:
263	        allowed = ", ".join(sorted(_JOIN_STRATEGIES))
264	        raise ValueError(
265	            f"invalid join_strategy: {join_strategy!r}; expected one of {allowed}"

284	class _Token:
285	    kind: str  # one of: keyword, ident, number, string, op, star, eof
286	    value: Any

290	_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(
291	    r"""
292	    \d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?   # 1, 1., 1.5, 1e3, 1.5e-2
293	    | \.\d+(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?         # .5
294	    """,
295	    re.VERBOSE,
296	)
297	# Bare identifiers: Unicode letters/underscore first, then word characters.
298	_IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\W\d]\w*", re.UNICODE)

300	
301	def _tokenize(sql: str) -> list[_Token]:
302	    if not isinstance(sql, str):
303	        raise QuerySyntaxError("SQL statement must be a string")
304	    tokens: list[_Token] = []
305	    i = 0
306	    n = len(sql)
307	    while i < n:
308	        ch = sql[i]
309	        if ch.isspace():
310	            i += 1
311	            continue
312	        if ch == "*":
313	            tokens.append(_Token("star", None, ch))
314	            i += 1
315	            continue
316	        if ch in ",()+-/":
317	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
318	            i += 1
319	            continue
320	        if ch in "=<>!":
321	            if ch == "!" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
322	                tokens.append(_Token("op", "!=", "!="))
323	                i += 2
324	                continue
325	            if ch in "<>" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
326	                op = ch + "="
327	                tokens.append(_Token("op", op, op))
328	                i += 2
329	                continue
330	            if ch in "=<>":
331	                tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
332	                i += 1
333	                continue
334	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character '!' at position {i}")
335	        if ch == "'":
336	            value, new_i = _tokenize_string(sql, i)
337	            tokens.append(_Token("string", value, sql[i:new_i]))
338	            i = new_i
339	            continue
340	        if ch == '"':
341	            value, new_i = _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql, i)
342	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(value, quoted=True))
343	            i = new_i
344	            continue
345	        if ch.isdigit() or ch == ".":
346	            match = _NUMBER_RE.match(sql, i)
347	            if match:
348	                text = match.group(0)
349	                tokens.append(_Token("number", _parse_number(text), text))
350	                i = match.end()
351	                continue
352	            # A '.' that does not start a number is the qualifier separator
353	            # used by two-table queries ("table.column").
354	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ".", ch))
355	            i += 1
356	            continue
357	        match = _IDENT_RE.match(sql, i)
358	        if match:
359	            text = match.group(0)
360	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(text, quoted=False))
361	            i = match.end()
362	            continue
363	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character {ch!r} at position {i}")
364	    tokens.append(_Token("eof", None, ""))
365	    return tokens

369	    lowered = word.lower()
370	    if not quoted and lowered in _KEYWORDS:
371	        if lowered == "true":
372	            return _Token("number", True, word)
373	        if lowered == "false":
374	            return _Token("number", False, word)
375	        return _Token("keyword", lowered, word)
376	    return _Token("qident" if quoted else "ident", word, word)

379	def _tokenize_string(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
380	    parts: list[str] = []
381	    i = start + 1
382	    n = len(sql)
383	    while True:
384	        j = sql.find("'", i)
385	        if j == -1:
386	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated string literal")
387	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
388	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == "'":
389	            parts.append("'")
390	            i = j + 2
391	            continue
392	        value = "".join(parts)
393	        try:
394	            value.encode("utf-8")
395	        except UnicodeEncodeError:
396	            raise QuerySyntaxError("string literal is not valid UTF-8") from None
397	        return value, j + 1

400	def _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
401	    parts: list[str] = []
402	    i = start + 1
403	    n = len(sql)
404	    while True:
405	        j = sql.find('"', i)
406	        if j == -1:
407	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated quoted identifier")
408	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
409	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == '"':
410	            parts.append('"')
411	            i = j + 2
412	            continue
413	        value = "".join(parts)
414	        if not value:
415	            raise QuerySyntaxError("quoted identifier must not be empty")
416	        return value, j + 1
417	
418	
419	def _parse_number(text: str) -> int | float:
420	    try:
421	        if any(ch in text for ch in ".eE"):
422	            value: int | float = float(text)
423	        else:
424	            value = int(text, 10)
425	    except ValueError:
426	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"invalid numeric literal {text!r}") from None
427	    if isinstance(value, int):
428	        # The magnitude 2**63 is accepted unsigned; the signed range check
429	        # happens after the optional leading sign is applied.
430	        if not (0 <= value <= 2**63):
431	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"integer literal {text} is outside the int64 range")
432	        return value
433	    if not math.isfinite(value):
434	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"float literal {text} must be finite")
435	    return value

438	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
439	# Parsed expression tree
440	#
441	# Node tuples:
442	#   ("literal", python_value, type_name)
443	#   ("column", name, table|None, table_quoted)        -- as parsed
444	#   ("column", name, index, type_name, nullable)      -- after binding
445	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node)              -- as parsed (+ - * /)
446	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node, type_name)   -- after binding
447	#   ("unary", operand, negate)                        -- as parsed
448	#   ("unary", operand, negate, type_name)             -- after binding
449	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None)   -- as parsed
450	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None, type_name) -- after binding
451	#   ("cmp", op, left_node, right_node)
452	#   ("isnull", operand, negate)
453	#   ("not", operand)
454	#   ("and"|"or", left, right)
455	# Predicate nodes are boolean-typed (three-valued at evaluation time);
456	# "literal"/"column"/"arith"/"unary" nodes are value nodes.
457	#
458	# Projection / ORDER BY reference items:
459	#   ("column_ref", name)                 -- a plain column name
460	#   ("agg", func_upper, arg_name|None)   -- an aggregate call; arg None = '*'
461	#   ("expr", alias)                      -- a computed scalar expression
462	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
463	
464	
465	@dataclass(frozen=True)
466	class _RefItem:
467	    """One projection element or ORDER BY key as parsed."""
468	
469	    kind: str  # "star" | "column" | "agg" | "expr"
470	    name: str | None = None  # column name, or the AS alias for kind == "expr"
471	    func: str | None = None  # uppercase function name for kind == "agg"
472	    arg: str | None = None  # aggregate column argument; "" stands for '*'
473	    expr: tuple | None = None  # parsed scalar expression for kind == "expr"
474	    descending: bool = False
475	    nulls_first: bool | None = None  # None -> default (NULLs last)
476	    # Table qualifiers (two-table queries only; None when unqualified):
477	    table: str | None = None
478	    table_quoted: bool = False
479	    arg_table: str | None = None
480	    arg_table_quoted: bool = False
481	
482	
483	@dataclass(frozen=True)
484	class _Join:
485	    """The single optional equi-join of a two-table query."""
486	
487	    kind: str  # "inner" | "left"
488	    table: str  # right table name as spelled
489	    table_quoted: bool
490	    left_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
491	    right_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
492	
493	
494	@dataclass
495	class _Select:
496	    items: tuple[_RefItem, ...]  # projection; may be a single ("star",) item
497	    table: str
498	    table_quoted: bool
499	    where: tuple | None
500	    # GROUP BY entries are (table|None, table_quoted, name) triples.
501	    group_by: tuple[tuple, ...] | None
502	    # Post-grouping boolean expression (aggregate queries only); None absent.
503	    having: tuple | None
504	    order_by: tuple[_RefItem, ...] | None
505	    limit: int | None
506	    join: _Join | None = None
507	    # SELECT DISTINCT: deduplicate the projected rows (non-aggregate only).
508	    distinct: bool = False
509	
510	    @property
511	    def star(self) -> bool:
512	        return len(self.items) == 1 and self.items[0].kind == "star"
513	
514	    @property
515	    def has_aggregate(self) -> bool:
516	        return any(item.kind == "agg" for item in self.items)
517	
518	    @property
519	    def is_aggregate_query(self) -> bool:
520	        return self.has_aggregate or self.group_by is not None or self.having is not None

522	
523	class _Parser:
524	    _CMP_OPS = frozenset(("=", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="))
525	
526	    def __init__(self, tokens: list[_Token], allow_join: bool = False):
527	        self.tokens = tokens
528	        self.pos = 0
529	        # Two-table statements (qualified names + one JOIN clause) are only
530	        # enabled for query_files; single-file entry points keep rejecting
531	        # them as syntax errors.
532	        self._allow_join = allow_join
533	
534	    def parse(self) -> _Select:
535	        select = self._parse_select()
536	        if self._peek().kind != "eof":
537	            tok = self._peek()
538	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected trailing input {tok.text!r}")
539	        return select
540	
541	    def _parse_select(self) -> _Select:
542	        self._expect_keyword("select")
543	        distinct = self._accept_keyword("distinct")
544	        items = tuple(self._parse_projection())
545	        self._expect_keyword("from")
546	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
547	        join = None
548	        if self._allow_join:
549	            if self._accept_keyword("inner"):
550	                self._expect_keyword("join")
551	                join = self._parse_join("inner")
552	            elif self._accept_keyword("left"):
553	                self._expect_keyword("join")
554	                join = self._parse_join("left")
555	        where = None
556	        if self._accept_keyword("where"):
557	            where = self._parse_or()
558	        group_by = None
559	        if self._accept_keyword("group"):
560	            self._expect_keyword("by")
561	            names = [self._parse_group_name()]
562	            while self._accept_op(","):
563	                names.append(self._parse_group_name())
564	            group_by = tuple(names)
565	        having = None
566	        if self._accept_keyword("having"):
567	            having = self._parse_having_or()
568	        order_by = None
569	        if self._accept_keyword("order"):
570	            self._expect_keyword("by")
571	            order_items = [self._parse_order_item()]
572	            while self._accept_op(","):
573	                order_items.append(self._parse_order_item())
574	            order_by = tuple(order_items)
575	        limit = None
576	        if self._accept_keyword("limit"):
577	            limit = self._parse_limit()
578	        return _Select(
579	            items=items,
580	            table=table_tok.value,
581	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
582	            where=where,
583	            group_by=group_by,
584	            having=having,
585	            order_by=order_by,
586	            limit=limit,
587	            join=join,
588	            distinct=distinct,
589	        )

591	    def _parse_join(self, kind: str) -> _Join:
592	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
593	        self._expect_keyword("on")
594	        left_key = self._parse_on_key()
595	        self._expect_op("=")
596	        right_key = self._parse_on_key()
597	        return _Join(
598	            kind=kind,
599	            table=table_tok.value,
600	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
601	            left_key=left_key,
602	            right_key=right_key,
603	        )
604	
605	    def _parse_on_key(self) -> tuple:
606	        tok = self._peek()
607	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
608	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
609	                f"ON requires table-qualified columns, got {tok.text!r}"
610	            )
611	        self._next()
612	        if not self._accept_op("."):
613	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
614	                "ON requires table-qualified columns (table.column)"
615	            )
616	        nxt = self._peek()
617	        if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
618	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
619	                f"expected column name after '.' in ON, got {nxt.text!r}"
620	            )
621	        self._next()
622	        return (tok.value, tok.kind == "qident", nxt.value)
623	
624	    def _parse_projection(self) -> list[_RefItem]:
625	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
626	        while self._accept_op(","):
627	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
628	        # Aliases are only supported for computed scalar expressions (which
629	        # consume their own "AS alias" in _parse_select_item); a trailing
630	        # identifier (including the spelling "as") where FROM is expected
631	        # names one on a bare column or aggregate.  Plain queries keep their
632	        # historical QuerySyntaxError classification; aggregate queries treat
633	        # the unsupported alias as a validation error.
634	        tok = self._peek()
635	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident") or (
636	            tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "as"
637	        ):
638	            grouped_ahead = any(
639	                t.kind == "keyword" and t.value == "group"
640	                for t in self.tokens[self.pos :]
641	            )
642	            if any(item.kind == "agg" for item in items) or grouped_ahead:
643	                raise QueryValidationError(
644	                    f"aliases are not supported; unexpected {tok.text!r} after projection item"
645	                )
646	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected FROM, got {tok.text!r}")
647	        return items
648	
649	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> _RefItem:
650	        tok = self._peek()
651	        if tok.kind == "star":
652	            self._next()
653	            return _RefItem("star")
654	        if (
655	            tok.kind == "ident"
656	            and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
657	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
658	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
659	        ):
660	            item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
661	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
662	                raise QueryValidationError(
663	                    "aggregate calls cannot be combined with scalar arithmetic"
664	                )
665	            return item
666	        node = self._parse_arith()
667	        if node[0] == "column":
668	            # A bare (possibly parenthesised) column reference keeps its
669	            # existing projection behaviour and needs no alias.
670	            return _RefItem(
671	                "column", name=node[1], table=node[2], table_quoted=node[3]
672	            )
673	        # A computed scalar expression must be named with AS.
674	        self._expect_keyword("as")
675	        alias = self._peek()
676	        if alias.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
677	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
678	                f"AS requires a result name, got {alias.text!r}"
679	            )
680	        self._next()
681	        return _RefItem("expr", name=alias.value, expr=node)
682	
683	    def _arith_op_ahead(self) -> bool:
684	        tok = self._peek()
685	        return tok.kind == "star" or (
686	            tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-", "/")
687	        )
688	
689	    def _parse_order_item(self) -> _RefItem:
690	        item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
691	        descending = False
692	        if self._accept_keyword("asc"):
693	            descending = False
694	        elif self._accept_keyword("desc"):
695	            descending = True
696	        nulls_first: bool | None = None
697	        if self._accept_keyword("nulls"):
698	            if self._accept_keyword("first"):
699	                nulls_first = True
700	            elif self._accept_keyword("last"):
701	                nulls_first = False
702	            else:
703	                tok = self._peek()
704	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
705	                    f"expected FIRST or LAST after NULLS, got {tok.text!r}"
706	                )
707	        return _RefItem(
708	            item.kind,
709	            name=item.name,
710	            func=item.func,
711	            arg=item.arg,
712	            descending=descending,
713	            nulls_first=nulls_first,
714	            table=item.table,
715	            table_quoted=item.table_quoted,
716	            arg_table=item.arg_table,
717	            arg_table_quoted=item.arg_table_quoted,
718	        )
719	
720	    def _qualifier_ahead(self) -> bool:
721	        nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
722	        return nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "."
723	
724	    def _parse_qualified_column(self) -> _RefItem:
725	        # Current token starts "table.column"; consumes all three tokens.
726	        table_tok = self._next()
727	        self._expect_op(".")
728	        name_tok = self._peek()
729	        if name_tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
730	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
731	                f"expected identifier after '.', got {name_tok.text!r}"
732	            )
733	        self._next()
734	        return _RefItem(
735	            "column",
736	            name=name_tok.value,
737	            table=table_tok.value,
738	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
739	        )
740	
741	    def _parse_column_or_agg(self) -> _RefItem:
742	        tok = self._peek()
743	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
744	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
745	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
746	            return self._parse_qualified_column()
747	        # A quoted identifier, or a bare word not spelled like an aggregate,
748	        # can only be a plain column reference.
749	        if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
750	            self._next()
751	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
752	        func = tok.value.lower()
753	        self._next()  # consume the function name
754	        if not self._accept_op("("):
755	            # e.g. a column literally named "count" -- the name token is
756	            # already consumed, so it is a plain column reference.
757	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
758	        arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted = self._parse_aggregate_args(func)
759	        self._expect_op(")")
760	        return _RefItem(
761	            "agg",
762	            func=func.upper(),
763	            arg=arg,
764	            arg_table=arg_table,
765	            arg_table_quoted=arg_table_quoted,
766	        )

768	    def _parse_aggregate_args(self, func: str) -> tuple:
769	        # Exactly one argument: '*' for COUNT, otherwise one (possibly
770	        # table-qualified) identifier.  Returns (name, table, table_quoted);
771	        # name "" stands for '*'.
772	        tok = self._peek()
773	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
774	            raise QueryValidationError(
775	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not a CASE expression"
776	            )
777	        if tok.kind == "star":
778	            if func != "count":
779	                raise QuerySyntaxError(f"{func.upper()} does not accept '*'")
780	            self._next()
781	            return ("", None, False)
782	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
783	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
784	                f"{func.upper()} requires one column argument, got {tok.text!r}"
785	            )
786	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
787	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
788	            nxt = self._peek()
789	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
790	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
791	                    f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
792	                )
793	            self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
794	            return (item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
795	        self._next()
796	        nxt = self._peek()
797	        if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
798	            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES:
799	                raise QueryValidationError(
800	                    f"aggregate functions must not be nested: "
801	                    f"{func.upper()}({tok.value.upper()}(...))"
802	                )
803	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
804	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
805	            )
806	        self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
807	        return (tok.value, None, False)
808	
809	    def _reject_expression_in_agg_arg(self, func: str) -> None:
810	        # Aggregate arguments stay limited to plain column references; a
811	        # scalar expression inside an aggregate query is a validation error.
812	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
813	            raise QueryValidationError(
814	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not an expression"
815	            )
816	
817	    def _parse_limit(self) -> int:
818	        tok = self._peek()
819	        if (
820	            tok.kind != "number"
821	            or isinstance(tok.value, bool)
822	            or not isinstance(tok.value, int)
823	        ):
824	            raise QuerySyntaxError("LIMIT requires an unsigned integer literal")
825	        self._next()
826	        if not (0 <= tok.value <= 2**63 - 1):
827	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
828	                f"LIMIT value {tok.value} is outside the allowed range"
829	            )
830	        return tok.value
831	
832	    def _expect_table_name(self) -> _Token:
833	        tok = self._peek()
834	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
835	            return self._next()
836	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected table name, got {tok.text!r}")
837	
838	    def _parse_group_name(self) -> tuple:
839	        # Returns a (table|None, table_quoted, name) triple.
840	        tok = self._peek()
841	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
842	            raise QueryValidationError(
843	                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not CASE expressions"
844	            )
845	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
846	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
847	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
848	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
849	            result = (item.table, item.table_quoted, item.name)
850	        else:
851	            self._next()
852	            result = (None, False, tok.value)
853	        # GROUP BY keeps accepting column references only; a scalar
854	        # expression in an aggregate query is a validation error.
855	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
856	            raise QueryValidationError(
857	                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not expressions"
858	            )
859	        return result

861	    # HAVING expression grammar ------------------------------------------------
862	    #
863	    # HAVING shares the WHERE boolean structure (NOT / AND / OR / comparison /
864	    # IS [NOT] NULL, parentheses, typed literals) but its value operands are
865	    # restricted to grouping columns, aggregate calls and literals; CASE,
866	    # scalar arithmetic and nested aggregates are rejected.
867	
868	    def _parse_having_or(self) -> tuple:
869	        node = self._parse_having_and()
870	        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
871	            node = ("or", node, self._parse_having_and())
872	        return node
873	
874	    def _parse_having_and(self) -> tuple:
875	        node = self._parse_having_comparison()
876	        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
877	            node = ("and", node, self._parse_having_comparison())
878	        return node
879	
880	    def _parse_having_comparison(self) -> tuple:
881	        left = self._parse_having_not_factor()
882	        tok = self._peek()
883	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
884	            self._next()
885	            right = self._parse_having_not_factor()
886	            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
887	        return left
888	
889	    def _parse_having_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
890	        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
891	            return ("not", self._parse_having_not_factor())
892	        return self._parse_having_postfix()
893	
894	    def _parse_having_postfix(self) -> tuple:
895	        node = self._parse_having_operand()
896	        # HAVING operands stay scalar references; arithmetic on top of a
897	        # group column or aggregate result is a validation error.
898	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
899	            raise QueryValidationError(
900	                "HAVING does not allow scalar arithmetic expressions"
901	            )
902	        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
903	            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
904	            self._expect_keyword("null")
905	            node = ("isnull", node, negate)
906	        return node
907	
908	    def _parse_having_operand(self) -> tuple:
909	        tok = self._peek()
910	        if self._accept_op("("):
911	            node = self._parse_having_or()
912	            self._expect_op(")")
913	            return node
914	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
915	            # Only a signed numeric literal is accepted; unary +/- around a
916	            # column or aggregate is scalar arithmetic and stays rejected.
917	            nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
918	            if nxt.kind == "number" and not isinstance(nxt.value, bool):
919	                self._next()
920	                self._next()
921	                value = nxt.value
922	                if isinstance(value, int):
923	                    if tok.value == "-":
924	                        value = -value
925	                    if not (_INT64_MIN <= value <= _INT64_MAX):
926	                        raise QuerySyntaxError(
927	                            "integer literal is outside the int64 range"
928	                        )
929	                    return ("literal", value, "int64")
930	                return ("literal", -value if tok.value == "-" else value, "float64")
931	            if nxt.kind == "eof":
932	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
933	                    f"expected a numeric literal after {tok.value!r} in HAVING"
934	                )
935	            raise QueryValidationError(
936	                "HAVING does not allow scalar arithmetic expressions"
937	            )
938	        if tok.kind == "star":
939	            raise QuerySyntaxError("'*' is not allowed in HAVING")
940	        if tok.kind == "number":
941	            self._next()
942	            value = tok.value
943	            if isinstance(value, bool):
944	                return ("literal", value, "bool")
945	            return (
946	                "literal",
947	                value,
948	                "int64" if isinstance(value, int) else "float64",
949	            )
950	        if tok.kind == "string":
951	            self._next()
952	            return ("literal", tok.value, "utf8")
953	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
954	            if (
955	                tok.kind == "ident"
956	                and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
957	                and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
958	                and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
959	            ):
960	                func = tok.value.lower()
961	                self._next()  # function name
962	                self._expect_op("(")
963	                arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted = self._parse_aggregate_args(func)
964	                self._expect_op(")")
965	                return ("hagg", func.upper(), arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted)
966	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
967	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
968	                return ("column", item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
969	            if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
970	                self._next()
971	                return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
972	            # An aggregate-style name not followed by '(' is a plain column.
973	            self._next()
974	            return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
975	        if tok.kind == "keyword":
976	            if tok.value == "case":
977	                raise QueryValidationError("CASE expressions are not allowed in HAVING")
978	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
979	                f"unexpected keyword {tok.text.upper()!r} in HAVING expression"
980	            )
981	        raise QuerySyntaxError(
982	            f"unexpected token {tok.text!r} in HAVING expression"
983	        )

985	    # WHERE expression grammar ------------------------------------------------
986	
987	    def _parse_or(self) -> tuple:
988	        node = self._parse_and()
989	        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
990	            node = ("or", node, self._parse_and())
991	        return node
992	
993	    def _parse_and(self) -> tuple:
994	        node = self._parse_comparison()
995	        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
996	            node = ("and", node, self._parse_comparison())
997	        return node
998	
999	    def _parse_comparison(self) -> tuple:
1000	        left = self._parse_not_factor()
1001	        tok = self._peek()
1002	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
1003	            self._next()
1004	            right = self._parse_not_factor()
1005	            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
1006	        return left
1007	
1008	    def _parse_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
1009	        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
1010	            return ("not", self._parse_not_factor())
1011	        return self._parse_postfix()
1012	
1013	    def _parse_postfix(self) -> tuple:
1014	        node = self._parse_arith()
1015	        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
1016	            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
1017	            self._expect_keyword("null")
1018	            node = ("isnull", node, negate)
1019	        return node

1021	    # Arithmetic expressions (numeric scalar operands) ------------------------
1022	    # Precedence (highest first): parentheses, unary +/-, * /, + -.
1023	
1024	    def _parse_arith(self) -> tuple:
1025	        node = self._parse_term()
1026	        while True:
1027	            tok = self._peek()
1028	            if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
1029	                self._next()
1030	                node = ("arith", tok.value, node, self._parse_term())
1031	            else:

1047	    def _parse_factor(self) -> tuple:

1065	                        )

1071	                nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "("
1072	            ) and not (nxt.kind == "keyword" and nxt.value == "case"):

1113	                tok.kind == "ident"
1114	                and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
1115	                and nxt.kind == "op"
1116	                and nxt.value == "("

1120	                )

1123	        if tok.kind == "keyword":
1124	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected keyword {tok.text.upper()!r} in expression")

1127	    def _parse_case(self) -> tuple:
1128	        # A searched CASE: at least one "WHEN cond THEN result", an optional
1129	        # "ELSE result", terminated by END.  Conditions are boolean
1130	        # expressions; results are scalar (numeric, bool or utf8) and may
1131	        # themselves contain nested CASE expressions.  The simple form
1132	        # (CASE value WHEN ...) is not supported.
1133	        branches: list[tuple] = []
1134	        while True:
1135	            self._expect_keyword("when")
1136	            condition = self._parse_or()
1137	            self._expect_keyword("then")
1138	            result = self._parse_arith()
1139	            branches.append((condition, result))
1140	            tok = self._peek()

1151	    def _peek(self) -> _Token:
1152	        return self.tokens[self.pos]
1153	
1154	    def _next(self) -> _Token:
1155	        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
1156	        self.pos += 1
1157	        return tok
1158	
1159	    def _accept(self, kind: str) -> bool:
1160	        if self._peek().kind == kind:
1161	            self.pos += 1
1162	            return True
1163	        return False
1164	
1165	    def _accept_op(self, value: str) -> bool:
1166	        tok = self._peek()
1167	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == value:
1168	            self.pos += 1
1169	            return True
1170	        return False
1171	
1172	    def _accept_keyword(self, value: str) -> bool:
1173	        tok = self._peek()
1174	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == value:
1175	            self.pos += 1
1176	            return True
1177	        return False
1178	
1179	    def _expect_keyword(self, value: str) -> _Token:
1180	        tok = self._peek()
1181	        if tok.kind != "keyword" or tok.value != value:
1182	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value.upper()}, got {tok.text!r}")
1183	        return self._next()
1184	
1185	    def _expect_op(self, value: str) -> _Token:
1186	        tok = self._peek()
1187	        if tok.kind != "op" or tok.value != value:
1188	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value!r}, got {tok.text!r}")

1393	        select.having is not None
1394	        and select.group_by is None
1395	        and not select.has_aggregate

1402	        )

1408	    group_indices: list[int] = []
